title: PR tidy: lightweight reviewer guides + personal notes
content:
Purpose:
A compact reference for my day-to-day PR reviews — a mix of heuristics, quick checks, and follow-up templates. Not intended as org policy (that lives in Confluence), but something I can copy into comments or use when pairing.

Quick principles (1-liners):
- Small PRs win: prefer slicing features into minimal, testable commits.
- Prefer readable over clever: choose explicitness when it reduces cognitive load.
- Surface intent in code + commit message: reviewers should not guess architecture choices.

Lightweight checklist (first pass):
[ ] Does the title/description explain the why and the risks? (link to design or ticket)
[ ] Is there a focused scope? If >400 lines, request split.
[ ] Tests: unit for logic, integration for critical flows. Does CI cover the new path?
[ ] Typing/contract: public APIs, exported functions documented / typed.
[ ] Backwards compatibility: feature flags, data migrations, consumer impact noted.
[ ] Performance: does change touch hot paths (routing, batching, KV cache)? Add microbenchmark or note expected impact.
[ ] Security/privacy: any PII or auth surface? If yes, flag to security.
[ ] Observability: metrics/traces/logs added for errors and latencies.
[ ] Rollout plan: canary, A/B, or immediate. Add fallback if risky.

Refactor heuristics (how I decide to accept):
- If a refactor is purely internal and has small test coverage delta -> approve with request to add a short migration/test in separate PR if possible.
- If it mixes refactor + feature: ask to split. If splitting is high cost, require a clear high-level rationale in description and a short follow-up plan.

Common comment snippets I reuse: (copy/paste)
- "High level: I like the direction. Can you add one sentence in the PR description that summarizes the risk surface and rollback plan?"
- "This is great; two nits: (1) small unit test for X, (2) please move the helper to module Y so it can be reused."
- "Looks risky to run across production traffic. Can we gate behind a flag (default off) and add a quick smoke test?"

Examples / mini patterns to call out:
- KV cache update: any change to cache keys needs explicit invalidation note and unit tests around cache miss/hit behavior.
- Serving hotpath change: prefer a microbenchmark snippet (bench script) showing before/after or at least an estimated token/sec delta.

Follow-up tracker (for me to leave in PR comments if not done):
- [ ] Add integration test that exercises failure path (ticket: INF-????)
- [ ] Create small runbook entry for this component if it affects restart behavior
- [ ] Schedule a 15m pairing to walk owners through the rollout and fallback plan

Open questions I often probe on review:
- "If this fails silently, what signals will alert us?"
- "Who owns the schema/contract for this surface and how will other teams be notified?"

Local TODOs (personal):
- Turn these heuristics into a 1-page cheatsheet for new reviewers (goal: shipping before Q2 onboarding).
- Bake a GH PR template that wires the basic checklist items for serving-runtime changes.
- Prototype a lint that flags >400 line PRs or mixed refactor/feature patterns.

Notes to self:
- Keep comments specific and actionable. Avoid "looks fine" without reason — better to say "no blocking issues, leaving two suggestions".
- If author is junior or new, prefer suggestions with links to examples rather than directives.

References & anchors:
- Ticket INF-1427 (context for recent batching change).
- PR 3124 (example where we forgot a metric and had to hotfix).

End of notes.
